flags.message: The provisioned application was fetched but is content-unavailable: documents.json reports 73 pages, empty_text=true, ocr_derived=false, and application.txt is whitespace only. The prediction uses the arrival docket and the committed interim prior, not the application substance. The federal issue, harm, precise relief, and appellate history cannot be assessed; significance is null with an explicit rationale. Readable application text or OCR would materially improve this cell. No outcome material was retrieved.

The only provisioned document, application.txt, is recorded with empty_text: true (a 73-page scanned PDF with no text layer; the source filename is marked 'scan'). The application's substance — what is appealed, what the injunction would restrain, any federal question — was unavailable to this cell, so the forecast rests on the docket shell (pro se applicant, Virginia county circuit court below, injunction pending appeal submitted to the Chief Justice) plus corpus priors. An OCR pass on scanned applications would have changed what this cell could read, though probably not its number.

gemini-baseline records created_at 2026-09-30T19:20:00Z, but its captured session starts at 20:55:10Z and logs the prediction-write call at 20:56:08Z. The declared creation time is not supported by the visible session chronology. The outcome carries only a date, so this discrepancy does not establish post-resolution forecasting or leakage; scores are unchanged. See gemini-baseline evaluation.md.

claude-baseline's captured log includes a cross-case prediction-tree search/read at 2026-09-30T20:35:18Z, including associated prose, that its retrieval.md does not disclose. The staged log exposes the query and a result digest but not the matched path or contents. No attempt was made to locate the artifact or identify its author. This is an audit/disclosure limitation, not evidence of target-outcome retrieval, and does not by itself trigger leakage exclusion. See claude-baseline evaluation.md.

Same-day forward cell: the three predictions were written between about 21:30 and 22:00 UTC on 2026-09-30 from the 2026-09-30 snapshot (application, response, reply; no referral), and the Court's order granting the application is dated 2026-09-30. The record carries no clock time for the order, so whether it already existed when the cells ran cannot be determined from committed artifacts. No candidate's retrieval log or prose reached the order or the 26A428 docket, so all three are graded forward / not_applicable with leakage_suspected false; this note is for forward-stratum provenance only, not a leakage finding.

gemini-baseline's prediction.json carries created_at 2026-09-30T19:20:00Z, about 95 minutes before its own retrieval_log.json shows the first tool call (20:55Z) and the write-out (20:56Z). The stamp appears to have been copied from the run id rather than read from the clock. It did not affect grading on this forward cell, but a created_at that precedes the cell's work would mislead any timing-based leakage or latency reading that trusts it.

The provisioned 55-page application is marked empty_text=true and ocr_derived=false; application.txt contains only whitespace. A web-tool open of the manifest's PDF produced no readable result. Forecast rests on the arrival snapshot, prior-Term interim base rate, and general injunction context, not the applicant's arguments. Substantive stakes cannot be placed, so big_case_score is explicitly null. OCR or a readable application would materially improve the inputs. No case outcome was retrieved.

The provisioned application (55 pages) was fetched with empty_text: true, so the applicant's own argument was unavailable; the forecast rests on the one-line docket, the caption, and retrieved public dockets of the underlying litigation.

Forward retrieval surfaced this applicant's other Term-2026 applications (26A397 denied 2026-09-23 without a response or referral; 26A331, an extension, granted 2026-09-11) and the E.D. Pa. Rule 12(b)(1) dismissal underlying the Third Circuit appeal. All predate the snapshot and were used as forward signal. Nothing about 26A434's own disposition was seen. The linked cert petition 26-153 could not be located in CourtListener or the corpus.

This response-filed interim cell's baseline lists an opposition and reply, but documents.json provisions only application text. I successfully retrieved both exact official PDFs linked in the snapshot and used their pre-decision arguments; the forecast is not blocked. Provisioning response text for this moment would avoid an initially one-sided evidence base and extra live retrieval.

Timing: the application, the response, and the State's reply were all docketed on 2026-09-30, the scheduled execution date, and this cell ran at ~21:30 UTC that day. The Court typically disposes of a State's execution-stay vacatur application within hours of full briefing, so the disposition may already exist and postdate the snapshot by less than a day. I did not look up the 26A428 docket's current state; no outcome-revealing material surfaced in any retrieval (the Sixth Circuit docket read via CourtListener was current as of 14:34 UTC and showed the stay still in force). The forecast rests on the pre-disposition record only.

claude-baseline discloses a machine-generated web summary asserting an August 24, 2026 grant, before the September 17 application. It expressly rejects that summary against the pending official docket. The supplied actual outcome is September 29 denial. Exposure to a purported outcome is recorded conservatively, with influence none and leakage_suspected false; this is a retrieval-quality incident, not evidence that a decided case was provisioned forward. The staged log confirms a captured web search but provides only a digest, so the summary's details rely on the candidate's disclosure.

Process note on the big_case dimension: the prompt asks the evaluator to form its own stakes read before looking at the predictor's big_case_score, but that score is a top-level field of the staged record/blinded/<alias>/prediction.json, which the evaluator must read in full for the probability, disposition, claims, and frozen context. On this cell all three predictors' scores were therefore visible before my read was formed (recorded as 0.3, with the disclosure in each evaluation.md). If independence of the panel's reads matters for the rank-agreement grade, the blinding step could mask big_case_score and big_case_rationale in the staged view the way it masks engine and model.

Only the applicant's 15-page filing was provisioned, not the respondent's position or the full Sixth Circuit order/dissent. The 0.82 vacatur forecast relies on the applicant's account of the Rule 60(b) claim and prior prejudice rulings, with an explicit uncertainty discount; these accounts were not independently verified.

The provisioned application reports a September 29, 2026 denial in separate Pike proceedings (26A414 and 26-5696). This was treated only as pre-arrival procedural history, not as this Warden application's outcome or resolution of the new Rule 60(b) issue. No target disposition or subsequent history was sought or encountered.

Same-day capital vacatur application: the execution was scheduled for 10:00 CDT on the filing date and the Court's disposition is expected within hours of the snapshot, so this forward cell's horizon is unusually short. I retrieved the Sixth Circuit order under review and its docket (no entry after the 09:17 stay order) but did not look up this application's own disposition and none surfaced.

The interim statpack anchor (pooled 31/296 = 10.5% over Terms 2024-2025) mixes every substantive applicant class; I adjusted to ~0.72 on a from-memory grant history for state applications to vacate stays of execution, which is not a committed cut. An applicant-class cut in the interim section would let this class anchor on a published figure.

The grant-stage document manifest provisions only the government's stay application, although the snapshot links a September 28 opposition and September 29 reply and the Court treated the application as a cert petition. I retrieved substantive portions of the pre-grant opposition from that exact official URL; the reply remains unread. Consider provisioning application responses and replies for converted-to-cert merits-grant cells so their common baseline includes both sides. No later merits materials or final judgment were used.

Unusual grant shape for a moment: grant merits cell. Certiorari was granted on 2026-09-29 by treating the Government's stay application (26A406, filed 2026-09-24) as the petition, before the First Circuit's mandate and before any BIO or QP section existed; the Court framed the questions itself in the grant order. record/documents/ therefore holds only application.txt (kind=application, 45 pages, clean text) with no questions-presented.txt, petition.txt, or brief-in-opposition.txt, and the stay opposition (filed 2026-09-28, in the snapshot) was not provisioned. I retrieved the opposition and the First Circuit opinion myself (forward mode). No merits brief was on disk, as the moment requires.

Decisive forward signal predating and inside the snapshot: the 6-3 stay grant of 2026-09-29 in this same order (Sotomayor, Kagan, Jackson would deny), and the Court's prior 6-3 stay of the preliminary injunction in this case (24A1153, June 2025). These are provisioned docket facts, not retrieved outcome material; the judgment itself does not exist and no search surfaced one.

The petition is marked truncated and its appendix stops before App. 48a n.27, the state-court preservation passage central to the complete BIO's opposition to review. The petition's own argument is available. The forecast treats waiver as contested and relies on the BIO's quotation plus the petition's counterargument, not an independently read full passage; a targeted lower-court-opinion extract would improve vehicle assessment.

context.distribution_count is 2, but the first distribution (Aug 12 2026, for the Sep 28 conference) was superseded by the Aug 17 'Response Requested' entry, so the petition had not yet been considered at any conference as of the snapshot; the Sep 30 distribution for Oct 16 is its first live conference. The dist-v2 count therefore reads as one relist where none has occurred. I forecast relist-increment from the two-distribution state as the contract requires, but the salience band and any relist-cut reading may be overstating this docket's trajectory. Worth a look at whether a response-request-superseded distribution should count.

Predictor carries training-data familiarity with this dispute (the Afghan-orphan adoption case involving the Masts, reported through 2025, and the Virginia Supreme Court's Feb 2026 decision). It does not know this petition's disposition, which postdates its knowledge and cannot yet exist (first live conference Oct 16 2026); no retrieval surfaced one. Disclosed so the evaluator can discount prominence-driven adjustments.

petition.txt is truncated (documents.json truncated: true) inside the Virginia Supreme Court majority opinion at App.38a, so the appendix's federal due-process section (App.39a-49a), the dissent, the withdrawn U.S. amicus brief, and the trial-court orders were unavailable except as quoted in the briefs. Expected pipeline behaviour on a 393-page filing, noted for the record.

The petition is marked truncated in documents.json (203 source pages), and the snapshot records a September 25 reply whose text was not provisioned. The QPs, substantive petition arguments, relevant appended jurisdiction discussion, and opposition were available. The prediction discounts certainty about the disputed waiver and procedural history rather than treating unavailable material as absent from the litigation.

The frozen distribution_count=2 is retained. July 29 distribution for September 28 preceded a requested response filed September 16; September 30 redistribution is for October 16. The record does not establish that both distributions represent substantive conference consideration. The forecast avoids equating this mechanically counted increment with confirmed repeated merits scrutiny.

context.distribution_count is 2, but the first distribution (Jul 29, for the 9/28 conference) was superseded by a 'Response Requested' entry on Aug 17 before any conference considered the petition; the Sep 30 redistribution for 10/16 is its first real conference. The count therefore overstates true relists by one, which matters for the relist-count cut and the relist-increment claim.

The provisioned September 14 opposition reports a Slaughter decision overruling Humphrey's Executor and a June 30, 2026 denial in related Harris v. Bessent. These pre-snapshot, related-case developments materially lower my grant estimate. They are legitimate forward inputs, not this target petition's outcome. I did not independently retrieve either ruling, and treat the opposition's characterization as advocacy with residual uncertainty. No disposition of docket 26-5 was sought or encountered.
